label: early original-phase o/i/p input after a w/s/e/t prefix
explanation: Fires about 97% of mass in the original (input) phase, mostly at t=1..4 (peak t=2-3), never at t=0 or the delimiter, and rarely in the copy phase. It needs a conjunction: the current input comes from a preferred set (o, i, p strongest, then 2, g, q, u, 3), and the prefix holds tokens from a second set (w strongest, then s, e, t, z, k, b; first_tok=w gives 6.9x lift). The largest activations are o/i/p right after a w-heavy prefix such as "w w o" or "z w w w p". Firing is weaker or absent when an o/i/p-type token was already seen earlier, and weaker in digit-heavy sequences. The behaviour looks graded and additive over the prefix tokens plus the current token, not a clean boolean, so the predicate only captures about half the mass (dev F1 0.40, mass recall 0.49).

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the first original token (most: w, s, e, z, t, k; least: 3, p, i, 1) and the current input token, by step (t=1: o, p, i, u; t=2: o, i, p, g; t=9: 2, p, i, h); timing cues that raise it most: t=3, t=2, recall_idx=1.
